claims.claim: The Passion of Irenaeus of Sirmium (Passio Irenaei episcopi Sirmiensis, catalogued as BHL 4466) is an anonymous Latin hagiographic text, opening 'Cum esset persecutio sub Diocletiano'.
Irenaeus was a young bishop of Sirmium in the Roman province of Pannonia (Pannonia Secunda), modern Sremska Mitrovica, who was martyred during the Great Persecution under Diocletian and Maximian.
The text recounts Irenaeus's interrogation before the provincial governor Probus, who demands that he sacrifice to the gods under the imperial decrees; Irenaeus refuses.
His wife, children and relatives plead with him to yield, and he stays firm, citing Christ's commandment (Matthew 10:37) that those who love relatives more than Christ are not worthy of him.

The author is anonymous; the text is considered to go back to the court interrogation (a court-record core), and it is classed among the so-called acta sincera, sober martyr accounts with factual outlook.

The Passion survives in two ancient versions, Greek and Latin, reflecting the bilingualism of Pannonia; which version is earlier is disputed, with the older view that Greek depends on Latin challenged by Manlio Simonetti.
